Cash balances include project escrow accounts protected under Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007. Disbursements require independent engineer certification against construction progress, insulating project assets from corporate creditors.
Off-plan revenue recognized strictly under IFRS 15 percentage-of-completion. Massive contracted backlog provides 2.5-3.5 years of forward revenue coverage.
Land bank held at historical acquisition cost; revalued market appraisal provides substantial asset cushion (>3.0x net debt).

verdict.stance: Neutral / Landbank & Growth Capex vs Negative OCF (BB- / Ba3)
verdict.summary: Dar Al Arkan posted 23.8% YoY revenue growth in 9M26 to SAR 3.47bn and SAR 788.4m net profit (+12% YoY) after redeeming its $400m Sukuk in 2025. Balance sheet equity sits at SAR 22.23bn (~38% net debt/equity), though operating cash flow remains negative on heavy international/domestic master development outlays.

positives: Proven USD sukuk market access: redeemed $400m Feb-26 sukuk and issued $600m 7.25% May 2031 sukuk (15th international issue).
9M 2026 net profit climbed 12% YoY to SAR 789.4m supported by property sales and investment income.
Large unencumbered Saudi land bank carried below market value provides substantial asset coverage.
negatives: Lumpy cash flow profile dependent on bulk land monetization timing and off-plan working capital cycles.
Elevated gross/net leverage (~3.5x) relative to Dubai peers (Emaar/Aldar/DAMAC).
International expansion via Dar Global (Oman, Dubai, Europe, Saudi Trump-branded projects) adds execution risk.
